about.title: Albany Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Albany is a small city, and the loss of even one life on its streets ripples through the whole community. Alameda County recorded one traffic death alongside dozens of injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, a reminder that busy corridors like I-80, Marin Avenue, Solano Avenue, and San Pablo Avenue carry real risk, especially during Friday afternoon rush between 3 and 5 p.m. If you've lost a spouse, domestic partner, child, or someone who depended on them financially, California law allows certain family members and heirs to pursue a wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal case that might follow the same crash. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects grieving families in Albany with an independent personal injury attorney who can explain your options, walk through the timeline, and help you understand what compensation may be available. You focus on your family; let someone else handle the legal groundwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Albany Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. An attorney can help clarify where you and your family stand before you take any action.

items.title: Watching the Clock
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity — such as a city or county road authority — may be involved. Given Albany's mix of local and county-maintained roads, this distinction can matter.

items.title: Recognizing What's Recoverable
items.desc: Wrongful death claims can account for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the harder-to-quantify loss of companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can help you understand which losses may apply to your family's specific situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after losing someone in Albany?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death for these claims. If a government entity, like a public road authority, played a role in the crash, that deadline is often much shorter. It's best to get guidance early so you don't lose the ability to pursue a claim.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. An independent attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies.

items.question: Does the location of the crash on a road like San Pablo or Solano Avenue affect our claim?
items.answer: It can matter for practical reasons, such as who maintains that stretch of roadway and whether a government entity might be a party to the case. It doesn't change the core elements of a wrongful death claim, but it can affect timing and evidence gathering.

items.question: Is this the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for your family's losses. It can proceed on its own timeline regardless of what happens in any related criminal prosecution.
